lesson_title: Tropical Cyclones: The Doughnut That Eats Coastlines
hook_text: Blue sky in the middle of a cyclone. Step outside now and you've made the deadliest mistake in weather.
clip_script: Then the eye: within an hour, near-calm and open sky. Pressure is at its minimum. The temptation to emerge is lethal, because the eye passes in twenty minutes to an hour and the far eye wall arrives with the full violence resumed — and with the wind blowing from the opposite direction, since you are now on the other side of a rotating system. Structures loosened by the first half are torn off by the reversed second half. It is the hole in the doughnut, not the end of the storm.
visual_style: First-person view inside a battered house: roaring rain, then sudden eerie sunshine, a hand reaching for the door — freeze frame, storm-anatomy doughnut diagram slams over the screen showing the far eye wall incoming.
pacing: Chaos, dead stop of silence at the eye, hard warning beat, rapid finish.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and learn the storm anatomy the exam draws every year.
